tier_reason: glyph/README.md carries a critcmp-style table (ab-glyph 11.1us vs rusttype 0.9 17.3us ttf, 98.1us otf; ratios 1.56 and 8.85 printed on the page) from May 2020 Criterion runs; the rusttype side matches rusttype's own dev/benches/layout.rs (same sentence, Exo2 fonts), but rustc version, CPU and machine are never stated and the current ab-glyph dev/benches/layout.rs no longer includes a rusttype run, so first-party with partial methodology.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 454 stars, 27 forks; ab_glyph crate about 45.2 million crates.io downloads (10.9 million recent), version 0.2.32
corrections.caveats: Baseline is rusttype 0.9, the crate ab_glyph replaced (same author added .otf support to rusttype), not HarfBuzz or FreeType; off the category's C/C++ baselines and the README does not compare with FreeType. Numbers are first-party and dated May 2020 (README notes performance has likely improved since); rustc version, CPU and machine are not stated; the workspace Cargo.toml currently sets [profile.bench] lto = "thin". The current dev/benches/layout.rs benchmarks ab_glyph only, so the rusttype column cannot be re-run from this repo; rusttype's own dev/benches/layout.rs (redox-os/rusttype mirror) has matching layout_a_sentence (exo2-ttf/otf) benches. The two harnesses are not identical: rusttype's bench calls font.layout (single line, kerning and advance) while ab-glyph's calls dev::layout_paragraph (kerning, advance plus wrapping at 600 px), so ab-glyph does slightly more work per glyph. Layout only; glyph rasterization speed is not compared. Both libraries do simple positioning, not OpenType shaping (no ligatures or GSUB/GPOS).

notes: Numbers and ratios match the README exactly; metadata (Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-08-30, active, not a fork) verified on github.com and glyph/Cargo.toml. Keep as an off-baseline Rust entry with the rusttype-only comparison flagged.

tier_reason: README table (5000 iterations, canvas-txt vs canvas-hypertxt with and without HyperWrapping) matches the record; the harness src/stories/benchmark.stories.tsx is public but browser, machine and OS are not stated and the timed work differs between libraries, so first-party with partial methodology.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Seconds for 5000 iterations, canvas-txt vs canvas-hypertxt vs canvas-hypertxt with HyperWrapping: 20 char 0.05 vs 0.05 vs 0.05; 100 char 0.59 vs 0.11 vs 0.11; 300 char 2.63 vs 0.40 vs 0.26; 600 char 6.17 vs 0.81 vs 0.47; 1000 char 11.19 vs 1.43 vs 0.77 (about 7.8x and 14.5x, derived from page data); 1800 char (overflow) 22.47 vs 2.29 vs 1.19 (about 9.8x and 18.9x, derived from page data). README also says HyperWrapping makes the measure pass over 100x faster (no numbers) and that canvas-hypertxt is 20-30% faster than canvas-multiline-text without HyperWrapping and about 1.2x with it (no table; canvas-multiline-text excluded for failing a correctness test).
corrections.workload: Storybook page in a browser: wrap and draw text into a 450 px wide box on a 500x500 canvas at 20px sans-serif, centered, for strings of 20 to 1800 characters (a fixed song-lyric prefix with the iteration number prepended), 5000 iterations per library; the timer wraps canvas-txt drawText versus canvas-hypertxt split plus fillText of each line.
corrections.caveats: Baseline is canvas-txt 3.x, a niche JavaScript library whose wrap search calls ctx.measureText once per added character; not HarfBuzz or FreeType, and canvas text wrapping is at the edge of the shaping and layout category. Browser, browser version, OS and machine are not stated. The harness (src/stories/benchmark.stories.tsx) is not symmetric: canvas-txt's drawText sets ctx.font inside the timed region on every call (twice, via getTextHeight) while canvas-hypertxt's font is set once before its loop (the README itself calls setting ctx.font 'really slow'); canvas-hypertxt stops drawing lines once y exceeds 500 px while canvas-txt draws every line, which favours canvas-hypertxt in the 1800-char overflow row; canvas-hypertxt's per-font width metrics and HyperWrapping model persist across the 5000 iterations (clearCache is called once before its loop), and HyperWrapping trades accuracy for speed (wraps can land one word early). Fonts rendered are the same (20px sans-serif) and fillText is timed for both. The README says it is not a drop-in replacement (no justify, no managed rendering). Last commit 2023-11-25 (stale). It is also the baseline that uWrap claims to beat.

notes: Numbers match the README; harness read and the canvas-txt v3.0.0 drawText source checked, which shows the speed gap is real (per-character measureText) but inflated somewhat by the timing asymmetries listed in caveats. Metadata (MIT, 138 stars, last commit 2023-11-25, stale) verified.

tier_reason: The only speed win (author's 4.5x over HarfBuzz) exists only in a search snippet of an unreachable X/blog post, so C at most; the reachable independent measurement (HarfBuzz discussion #5375, Google Benchmark perf/benchmark-shape.cc with HarfBuzz's kbts shaper backend src/hb-kbts.cc) shows kb slower everywhere but states no CPU, compiler, flags or kb version and comes from the competing project's maintainer.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No speedup verified; flagged not-faster. HarfBuzz maintainer's run (discussion #5375, 2025-07-23, benchmark-shape, 'ot' shaper vs 'kbts' backend): Roboto-Regular en-thelittleprince.txt 9.11 ms vs 26.5 ms (HarfBuzz 2.9x faster); Roboto-Regular en-words.txt 11.3 ms vs 38.4 ms (3.3x); Amiri-Regular 40.6 ms vs 48.3 ms (kb about 20% slower); Gulzar-Regular Urdu 782 ms vs 5198 ms (kb 6.6x slower); Gulzar-Regular second text 24.9 ms vs 4021 ms (kb 160x slower); NotoSansDevanagari-Regular 25.3 ms vs 50.5 ms (kb 2x slower). Font loading (benchmark-font): Roboto 23.6 us vs 1000 us (40x), Gulzar 310 us vs 235,940 us (760x), NotoSansDevanagari 34.0 us vs 4,335 us (128x). The author's opposite claim (kb on average 4.5x faster than HarfBuzz on HarfBuzz's test suite plus own tests, Ryzen 9 5900HX, clang 20, Linux) is search-snippet only.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Author's claim (search snippet only): clang 20 on Linux, flags not stated. HarfBuzz maintainer run: compiler, flags and build type not stated (HarfBuzz perf/README.md gives meson debugoptimized as the default benchmark build).
corrections.hardware: Author's claim (search snippet only): Ryzen 9 5900HX. HarfBuzz maintainer run: CPU not stated.
corrections.caveats: Disputed speed claim, kept as a flagged not-faster entry. A WebSearch snippet attributed to the author (X post and developer blog, unreachable here; mastodon.gamedev.place is egress-blocked) says kb is on average 4.5x faster than HarfBuzz at shaping on HarfBuzz's test suite extended with the author's tests, Ryzen 9 5900HX, clang 20, Linux; no per-test numbers or harness were found on any reachable page, and the kb README and header carry no benchmarks. The only opened comparison is by HarfBuzz maintainer Behdad Esfahbod (an interested party) on 2025-07-23 in harfbuzz discussion #5375, using HarfBuzz's public Google Benchmark harness (perf/benchmark-shape.cc, which iterates every compiled-in shaper; test fonts and texts listed in its default_tests) and the kbts backend (src/hb-kbts.cc, written by HarfBuzz's Khaled Hosny, enabled by meson option kbts; HarfBuzz 11.4.0 NEWS says it is 'purely for testing and performance evaluation'). That run found kb slower on every font (2x to 160x) and 40x to 760x slower at font loading, and reported crashes in the HarfBuzz test suite and an infinite loop or very slow run on SourceSerifVariable-Roman.ttf; CPU, compiler, flags and kb version were not stated, and timings go through HarfBuzz's buffer API wrapper. A third-party user (kb issue #21, 2025-07-13, libraqm harness, NotoSansArabic and NotoSans, 309 codepoints) also measured kb about 2x slower than raqm/HarfBuzz; the issue's 42 comments were not visible. kb is now v2.28e (2026-10-02), much newer than the July 2025 release measured, and HarfBuzz pins kb revision ca6c962 in subprojects/kbts.wrap, so re-running benchmark-shape with -Dkbts=enabled would settle the current state. Maintainer also notes no cluster information (display-only shaper) and no variable-font support.

notes: Discussion #5375 opened and its numbers recorded as the independent measurement (kb slower everywhere); the 4.5x claim is snippet-only and not fabricated as far as can be told, so no reject. Metadata (Zlib, 1.2k stars, last commit 2026-10-02, active, header v2.28e) verified.
